parsed.notes: Reviewed all seven inventory rows under lens B only; no support or quote-fidelity merits finding is made.

reasons: Lake identity verifies Coolidge v. New Hampshire as a U.S. Supreme Court decision dated 1971-06-21 with official citation 403 U.S. 443.
Lake treatment marks the case as caution, not overruled or dead; its scope note says surviving requirements remain.
residual_risks: Treatment derivation lists proposed negative events and audit_needed, but the disclosed judgment field remains caution.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: When citing as live law, pair the citation with the Horton limitation.

reasons: Lens B does not test home-role support merits.
No disclosed final treatment field defeats using Coolidge on the Plain View Doctrine page if the Horton limitation is preserved.
residual_risks: The role should not be read to make the abandoned inadvertence prong current law.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: On the home page, label Coolidge as origin/limited rather than an unqualified current test.

defect.evidence_quote: Horton v. California (1990) abandoned the inadvertence requirement of the Coolidge plurality's plain-view formulation; the prior-justification and immediately-apparent requirements survive.
defect.problem: The holding/proposition survives only if framed as the Stewart plurality origin, not as an unqualified current modern plain-view test, because the disclosed treatment says Horton abandoned the inadvertence requirement.
defect.proposed_fix: Add an explicit caveat in the holding field: origin/Stewart plurality; inadvertence later abandoned by Horton, while prior-justification and immediately-apparent requirements survive.

reasons: Lake field_i_validity is caution and varies_by_point is true.
The treatment scope note limits only the inadvertence part and preserves the prior-justification and immediately-apparent requirements.
residual_risks: Support and quote fidelity are outside lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Make the treatment caveat inseparable from the holding summary.

reasons: Lens B does not test home-role support merits.
The disclosed treatment limitation concerns the plain-view inadvertence requirement, not a final overruling of Coolidge's neutral-magistrate relevance.
residual_risks: No separate point-specific treatment record is disclosed for the neutral-and-detached-magistrate point.

reasons: The content treatment override matches the lake point_override: field_i_validity caution, s3_binding_status provisional, and Horton v. California, 496 U.S. 128, field_ii limited.
The lake scope note states the same limited point: Horton abandoned inadvertence while other requirements survive.
residual_risks: The override is marked provisional in the disclosed record.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the provisional status visible wherever this point override is rendered.

reasons: The payload matches the lake treatment judgment: field_i_validity caution, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point true, and the Horton scope note.
The disclosed lake record supports caution rather than a complete overruling.
residual_risks: Lake derivation reports audit_needed and proposed negative events, so the treatment call depends on the disclosed judgment field rather than completed edge audit.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid rendering the global status as merely limited without also showing the field_i_validity caution label.

reasons: Lake identity court and court_level are U.S. Supreme Court/scotus.
A caution/limited treatment status does not defeat Binding — SCOTUS for surviving requirements.
residual_risks: Binding weight should be understood as limited to surviving requirements after Horton.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Render as Binding — SCOTUS for surviving requirements when paired with the treatment badge.
